name: Apply for Maternity Allowance (online, reviewed)
description: The private beta online journey for Maternity Allowance, Inc 3.0 MVP, modelled from the DWP journey board MA Citizen Journey 3.0 + OL. Serves claimants in the beta postcode area who were employed during their Test Period and have not lived or worked outside the UK. Employment history and earnings are read from HMRC RTI and confirmed rather than transcribed. Converted to the canonical schema: onward routing uses transitions, so the forks in the journey are shown, but the conditions and outcome labels that decide each fork were not in the source and are not set here, so the graph shows where the journey branches without saying which branch is taken. The paper MA1 handover reached by eleven of the fourteen exits, the twenty minute session timeout, and the evidence upload mechanism still cannot be referenced. This copy is being reviewed branch by branch against the maternity-allowance-online.json original, confirming or fixing each fork one at a time rather than editing the original in place.
descriptionPublic: Apply online for Maternity Allowance if you are employed but cannot get Statutory Maternity Pay. You will need a GOV.UK One Login account and evidence of your pregnancy.

type.body: Maternity Allowance are payments you can get when you take time off to have a baby. You could get it if you are employed but cannot get Statutory Maternity Pay, are self-employed, have recently stopped working, or take part in unpaid work for the business of your spouse or civil partner. You can get Maternity Allowance for up to 39 weeks and can claim after the 26th week of the pregnancy. If you claim later than 3 months after your entitlement starts, you may not get the full amount. Before you start you will need to upload evidence of your maternity certificate (MAT B1), an SMP1 form from each employer you had during the 15th week before the week your baby is due, your baby's birth certificate if applicable, and your baby's still birth or death certificate if applicable. You'll need a GOV.UK One Login account. Maternity Allowance may affect other benefits or entitlements you are getting, including Universal Credit. We will delete your answers if you do not do anything for 20 minutes and you will have to start again.

type.body: Your Universal Credit payments will be reduced by an amount equal to your Maternity Allowance payments. You may get an extra amount of Universal Credit for your children whether you get Maternity Allowance or not. If you claim Maternity Allowance you get Class 1 National Insurance credits. If you claim Universal Credit only, you get Class 3 credits, which count towards State Pension only.

type.body: This is the employment information we have from HM Revenue & Customs for your Test Period. Your Test Period is the 66 weeks before the week your baby is due, not the actual date of birth. You may be able to get Maternity Allowance if you were employed for at least 26 weeks in your Test Period. These do not need to be 26 continuous weeks. You must provide your employment history for your Test Period before you can get Maternity Allowance.

type.body: You'll need an SMP1 form from your employer to get Maternity Allowance. If you have more than 1 employer, you must send us an SMP1 form from each employer. If your employer refuses to give you an SMP1 form, you can contact HM Revenue & Customs for help. You can still continue with your application without your SMP1 form. We'll contact you later and you'll need to send it to us through post.

type.body: Based on your HMRC records, your earnings may result in you getting the full amount of Maternity Allowance. Your application will need to be reviewed before Maternity Allowance can be awarded. These payslips show the money you earned during your Test Period and come from HM Revenue & Customs. You need 13 weeks of payslips of your highest earning weeks. They do not need to be linked together.

type.body: Your answers so far have been saved. You can check each section you have completed if you need to change anything. Before you can be awarded any Maternity Allowance you will need to submit the outstanding evidence. You can submit it now, or DWP will contact you and you will need to send it through the post. You can still submit your application without uploading your evidence.

type.body: If you have given a mobile number we have sent you an SMS to confirm your application. We will send you a letter when we have made a decision. We may call or write if we need more information. If we have everything we need you should get a decision within 20 working days.

type.body: The other benefits that can be affected are bereavement benefits, Carer's Allowance, Carer Support Payment in Scotland, Employment and Support Allowance, Income Support, and Jobseeker's Allowance, which will stop if you get Maternity Allowance. Most benefits are paid every 2 or 4 weeks and may fall on different days. If you are getting Statutory Sick Pay on or after the 4th week before the week the baby is due, this will stop.
